rows.section: Attachment B — Limitations item (1) ('Optional Services'), example c)
rows.notes: Full item as returned: 'Services that are more expensive than the form of treatment customarily provided under accepted dental practice standards are called "Optional Services." Optional Services also include the use of specialized techniques instead of standard procedures. Examples of Optional Services: a) a crown where a filling would restore the tooth; b) an inlay/onlay instead of an amalgam restoration; c) porcelain, resin or similar materials for crowns placed on a maxillary second or third molar, or on any mandibular molar (an allowance will be made for a porcelain fused to high noble metal crown); or d) an overdenture instead of denture. If an Enrollee receives Optional Services, an alternate Benefit will be allowed, which means We will base Benefits on the lower cost of the customary service or standard practice instead of on the higher cost of the Optional Service.' IMPORTANT for the engine: for molar crowns the alternate basis is a porcelain-fused-to-high-noble-metal crown allowance, which is not a dollar amount printed here -> plan payment is an upper bound. Existing DD24 condition 'mandibular_molar' omits maxillary second/third molars.
